<h2 id="toc-1">Official announcement: Core Web Vitals update delayed to mid-June</h2>
<p>Google issued an official announcement stating that the Core Web Vitals update that many people have been waiting for will be changed from the original May date to<strong>will be gradually launched in mid-June and is expected to be completed by the end of August this year.</strong>. Regarding CWVs, it has been introduced many times since the announcement. If you are still confused about this, you can refer to it.
Articles written before by<a class="rank-math-link" href="./core-web-vitals-lcp-fid-cls.html"></a>, and the ones mentioned above<a class="rank-math-link" href="./seo-newsletter-issue-29.html#toc-9">Official Q&amp;A</a>。</p>
<p>In addition, a new "Webpage Experience" report has been added to GSC, including all webpage experience scores except CWVs. Regarding the above scores, you can refer to this new<a class="rank-math-link" href="https://support.google.com/webmasters/answer/10218333">official document</a>。</p>

<h2 id="toc-3">GSC will allow users to report indexing issues (US Only)</h2>
<p>Google will allow users to report web indexing issues through GSC or through<a class="rank-math-link" href="https://support.google.com/webmasters/contact/indexing_issue_form">this form</a>. The announcement states that it is only open to users in the United States. It is not sure whether other countries can open the form or apply it.</p>
<blockquote class="embed embed--twitter"><p>Twitter／X Post</p><a href="https://twitter.com/googlesearchc/status/1387460807831683072" rel="noopener noreferrer">View original post on Twitter／X</a></blockquote>
<p>"The webpage is not indexed" and "the webpage is not ranked" are two different things. I have encountered situations that are called "not indexed", but almost all of them are actually not ranked; or there is an error in the webpage itself, and the GSC<a class="rank-math-link" href="https://support.google.com/webmasters/answer/9012289#missing_page">web page detection tool</a>can identify most of the errors. I personally think that there are not many opportunities for the reward mechanism launched this time to really come in handy.</p>
<hr class="wp-block-separator"/>
</div>
<div class="wp-block-group">
<h2 id="toc-4">Google 2020 Webspam Report</h2>
<p>Google recently released its annual webspam report, telling everyone about some of their progress in combating spam. An incredible number is that they find 40 billion spam web pages every day! The report talks about their simple process -First of all, Google will have a system in the crawling stage to prevent spam content from being included; if spam content is accidentally included, the ranking mechanism will also prevent them from being ranked at the top of the search results, and use this information to optimize the machine learning model in the crawling phase; and finally, manual review.</p>
<p>In addition to spam content, starting in 2020, Google has also expanded its crackdown on other types of harmful content, including fraud, slander, etc., including the recent<a href="./seo-newsletter-issue-30.html#toc-2">"Product Reviews" update</a>。</p>
<div class="wp-block-image"><figure class="aligncenter size-large is-resized"><img alt="Illustration for SEO e-Newsletter Issue 31 – 2021.04.16~2021.04.30" class="wp-image-2722" decoding="async" height="290" loading="lazy" src="./wp-content/uploads/2021/04/WebspamReport2020_EverySteps-1024x657.png" width="452"/><figcaption>Spam prevention process</figcaption></figure></div>
<p>Google produces such a report every year. Digital Engine has also introduced reports in the past few years. Welcome to read!</p>
<p>link:<a class="rank-math-link" href="https://developers.google.com/search/blog/2021/04/how-we-fought-search-spam-2020">2020 report</a></p>
<hr class="wp-block-separator"/>

<h2 id="toc-5">iProspect Statistics: CWV scores by industry</h2>
<p>iProspect, a subsidiary of Dentsu Group, made this statistics. It took the top 100 traffic websites in 15 industries in the UK, a total of 1,500 websites, and analyzed their<a class="rank-math-link" href="./core-web-vitals-lcp-fid-cls.html">Core Web Vitals Score</a>。</p>
<p>According to this analysis, overall only 20% of websites meet the "good" standard. Among them, government websites have the highest average score, and fashion websites have the lowest score. It seems that the general website is not ready for this update.</p>

<h2 id="toc-8">[Official article] Why does Google remove web pages from search results?</h2>
<p>Danny Sullivan is at<a class="rank-math-link" href="https://blog.google/products/search/when-and-why-we-remove-content-google-search-results/">this article</a>explains a problem that most people rarely encounter and don't want to encounter: "How to get a webpage to be removed from Google?", which is generally divided into three situations.</p>
<p>1. <strong>Legal factors (ex: copyright, legality)<br/></strong>Google is not a law enforcement agency, and laws vary from region to region. Therefore, disputes such as copyright, original content, etc. need to be adjudicated by law enforcement agencies and notified to Google to remove the content. Rather than complaining, Google will investigate, unless it is an obvious violation of the law such as child pornography or drugs.</p>
<div class="wp-block-image"><figure class="aligncenter size-large is-resized"><img alt="Illustration for SEO e-Newsletter Issue 31 – 2021.04.16~2021.04.30" class="wp-image-2529" decoding="async" height="249" loading="lazy" src="./wp-content/uploads/2021/01/%E4%BE%B5%E6%AC%8A%E4%B8%8B%E6%9E%B6Google%E6%90%9C%E5%B0%8B-1024x498.png" width="512"/><figcaption><em><a class="rank-math-link" href="https://lumendatabase.org/notices/18982842">Example</a>: The website "Mr. Crazy" accused another webpage of plagiarism, causing the webpage to be removed from Google Search.</em></figcaption></figure></div>
<p><strong>2. Personal appeal<br/></strong>Although Google does not take the initiative to accept things that require legal rulings, if personal confidential information is leaked, for example, a large number of villagers dig out someone's ID card number, contact information, and medical records and put them online, you can still file a complaint<a class="rank-math-link" href="https://support.google.com/websearch/troubleshooter/9685456">Google complaint</a>requested removal. However, if it is a negative review of the business or content that is suspected of defamation, it may not be accepted.</p>
<p><strong>3. Scale</strong><br/>To be able to handle massive complaints, it is necessary to establish a scalable and automated mechanism. Google will use complaints to optimize its quality control system. For example, if a website has a large number of copyright violation notices, Google will use this as a quality signal to adjust the anonymity and exposure of the website in search results.</p>
<p>link:<a class="rank-math-link" href="https://blog.google/products/search/when-and-why-we-remove-content-google-search-results/">official article</a></p>
<hr class="wp-block-separator"/>
</div>

<h2 id="toc-9">[Video] SEO Current Situation Analysis from Internet Yearbook Report</h2>
<p><a class="rank-math-link" href="https://almanac.httparchive.org/en/2020/table-of-contents">Web Almanac</a>(Internet Yearbook) is a report produced every year by the organization HTTP Archive. This year is the second year. This video features Aleyda Solis describing some of the findings in the SEO chapter, such as...</p>
<ul><li>99% of web pages use title tags, the median is six words, 38 characters (last year it was only 20 characters!)</li><li>Only about 68% of web pages have meta description</li><li>is used in about 28~30% of web pages<code>rel=nofollow</code>is on the link, but<code>rel=ugc</code>and
The usage rate of<code>rel=sponsored</code>is only around 0.3%</li><li>HTTPS usage has reached 73~77%, 10% higher than last year</li><li>Less than 1% of web pages use AMP</li></ul>
<figure class="embed embed--youtube"><div class="embed__frame"><iframe allow="accelerometer; autoplay; clipboard-write; encrypted-media; gyroscope; picture-in-picture; web-share" allowfullscreen="" loading="lazy" referrerpolicy="strict-origin-when-cross-origin" src="https://www.youtube-nocookie.com/embed/xpSRdok0qUM" title="YouTube video player"></iframe></div><figcaption><a href="https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=xpSRdok0qUM" rel="noopener noreferrer">View original video on YouTube</a></figcaption></figure>
<p>The above is only a small part. In addition to SEO, this Internet Yearbook report contains CSS, JavaScript, SEO, Performance, CMS, Ecommerce... a total of 22 chapters. There are also some interesting information in other chapters, such as<a class="rank-math-link" href="https://almanac.httparchive.org/en/2020/cms">CMS</a>and
In the chapter of<a class="rank-math-link" href="https://almanac.httparchive.org/en/2020/ecommerce">Ecommerce</a>, you can see what the most common content or e-commerce platforms are now, the average CWV score of each, the usage rate of AMP... etc. It is recommended that you check it out when you have time.</p>

<h2 id="toc-10">[Video] How does Google Search Console record rankings?</h2>
<p>How are rankings recorded in GSC - is it the value seen by actual users, or is it a theoretical ranking? If the same website appears more than once in the search results, how is it calculated? John Muller gives the answer in this video.</p>
<figure class="embed embed--youtube"><div class="embed__frame"><iframe allow="accelerometer; autoplay; clipboard-write; encrypted-media; gyroscope; picture-in-picture; web-share" allowfullscreen="" loading="lazy" referrerpolicy="strict-origin-when-cross-origin" src="https://www.youtube-nocookie.com/embed/l3l9gB7G4zU" title="YouTube video player"></iframe></div><figcaption><a href="https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=l3l9gB7G4zU" rel="noopener noreferrer">View original video on YouTube</a></figcaption></figure>
<p>The answers to the above two questions are "<em>actual value</em>" and "<em>takes the highest ranking</em>". The ranking is calculated in<a class="rank-math-link" href="https://support.google.com/webmasters/answer/7042828">official document
There is a very detailed explanation in</a>. Some interesting questions include "How to record the exposure of a webpage that appears in People Also Ask?", "How to record the ranking of a webpage that appears in the carousel?"... etc. You can find the answers. I recommend everyone to read it!</p>
